key_insight: A graded Cr3C2-NiCr detonation coating outperformed a homogeneous coating by creating a denser layered barrier that better resists corrosive attack.
engineering_relevance: Designing composition gradients in detonation-sprayed coatings can substantially improve service life for steel components exposed to aggressive environments.
method: Applied Cr3C2-NiCr (75/25, 10–45 µm) to 12Kh1MF steel using CCDS2000 detonation spraying
Compared a homogeneous coating at constant 57% gas mixture filling ratio with a gradient coating formed by 57→64→73% sequential filling ratios
Evaluated microstructure, phase composition, polarization behavior, and long-term corrosion in Na2SO4 and HCl mist with CuCl2·2H2O
evidence_signal: The gradient coating shifted polarization curves to lower current densities and showed no visible corrosion after 1000 h, versus first corrosion at 456 h and 1.14% mass loss for the homogeneous coating.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on a specific steel, powder chemistry, and detonation-spraying schedule, so the gradient recipe may need re-optimization for other substrates or operating conditions.
paper_title: Study of the Corrosion Resistance of Cr3C2-NiCr-Based Gradient Detonation Coatings
